svg.text: A funnel from the question of machine consciousness, through the psychological biases that make us believe in it,
into four separate doubts about computation, opening into two live ethical worries that sit side by side rather
than resolving, and finally looping back to the opening question of what makes us human.

g.text: Doubt accumulates down the page until it forks into two risks we must hold at once, then the essay returns to its

g.title: Old fantasies, new claims — golem to Lemoine's chatbot — From Frankenstein to a Google engineer's claim that a chatbot had feelings — the dream keeps resurfacing. — → spya-d9a0wr
Why it matters — rights, our psychology, self-knowledge — If AI is conscious it may have moral status; if we only feel it is, our own minds and ethics are at stake either way. — → spya-e68t9h
Three human-centered biases — human as template, human as pinnacle — Anthropocentrism, human exceptionalism and anthropomorphism combine to make us see minds where there may be none. — → spya-cvaqgs
g.text: human as template, human as pinnacle

g.title: Fluent language seems minded — 'hallucinate' implies real experience — Chatbots get called conscious far more than AlphaFold, because language is central to our sense of human specialness. — → spya-k6fpme

Exponential hype & techno-rapture — feels like an inflection point — Exponential change always feels like a turning point, and dreams of digital immortality make conscious AI an alluring story. — → spya-cke6sj
Just pattern-seeing — pareidolia — not proof of mind — Like seeing a face in a cinnamon bun: recognizing the illusion is only the first step. — → spya-k850tu
Brains aren't computers — no software/hardware split — → spya-sk4su6
Other kinds of computing matter — analogue, dynamical processes — → spya-affgsh
Life itself may matter — living, self-sustaining bodies — → spya-e7jqx4
Simulating isn't creating — a modeled storm isn't wet — → spya-cqh5wq
Functionalism looks shaky — not disproven, just unsupported — Four independent lines of doubt, each standing on its own, reinforce one another. — → spya-uzr60x
Don't deliberately build real conscious AI — new suffering we couldn't control — → spya-yverz7
AI that merely seems conscious is already risky — distinct from the question of real consciousness — → spya-x63ycg

g.title: Our biases risk false positives, not false negatives — unlike with animals, surface likeness misleads us — → spya-d89xf7
g.text: Our biases risk false positives, not false
unlike with animals, surface likeness misleads us

g.title: More breath than thought, more meat than machine — an embodied self, not a soul uploaded — The essay closes by recovering an older, embodied sense of what makes us us. — → spya-w8z40d
g.text: an embodied self, not a soul uploaded
Why We're Tempted To Believe It
Several separate psychological biases feed into one another, all ending at the same place: a mind projected onto a
machine, no stronger than an optical illusion.

g.title: Intelligence ≠ consciousness — but we assume they travel together — → spya-nj888h

Four separate arguments, each with its own supporting case, converge on the same weak point: the assumption that
computation alone is enough for consciousness.
